name: Views Contact Form
description: Field formatter for email fields that renders an inline site-wide contact form whose recipient is the field's email value.
provides_plugin_types: Field formatter: views_contact_form_email_formatter (for email field types)
project_description: Views Contact Form (2.0.x) provides a single field formatter, 'views_contact_form_email_formatter', for core email field types. Instead of printing an email address (as a plain value or a mailto: link), the formatter renders a full core contact-message form inline in the field's place, and sets the form's recipients to the email value(s) held by the field being formatted. It is designed for use on any entity display or in a Views 'field' row where an email field is shown, so a listing (of users, nodes, referenced entities, etc.) can present a per-row 'send a message to this address' form. The admin picks which non-personal contact form (feedback, or any custom contact form) supplies the form's fields and settings, and can optionally also add that contact form's own configured recipients alongside the field value. The rendered form reuses core's contact_message entity form (Drupal\contact\MessageForm), so subject/message fields, the authenticated-user name/mail lock, copy-to-self restriction for anonymous users, and core contact flood control all still apply. NOTE: the installed 2.0.x code is far smaller than the drupal.org project page (which still describes the Drupal 7 era Views style/handler and Honeypot/Mollom submodules) - none of those exist in 2.0.x; only the email field formatter ships. NOTE: the module hard-depends on the core Contact module at runtime (it loads ContactForm and creates contact_message entities) but its info.yml only declares a dependency on Views, so Contact must be enabled manually.
